s1.syndrome_frame: Acute to subacute onset of unilateral facial paresis and numbness with severe headaches and signs of orbital and sinus involvement
key_facts: Previous treatment with unknown antibiotic without steroids
Nasal endoscopy showed polypoid changes of right middle turbinate and purulence
CT scan showed orbital abscess extending from right-sided rhinosinusitis
White blood cell count at high end of normal
Cultures grew coagulase-negative Staphylococcus aureus and Enterococcus faecalis

raw.syndrome_frame: Acute to subacute onset of unilateral facial paresis and numbness with severe headaches and signs of orbital and sinus involvement
key_facts: Previous treatment with unknown antibiotic without steroids
Nasal endoscopy showed polypoid changes of right middle turbinate and purulence
CT scan showed orbital abscess extending from right-sided rhinosinusitis
White blood cell count at high end of normal
Cultures grew coagulase-negative Staphylococcus aureus and Enterococcus faecalis

shortlist.label: Orbital cellulitis
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has orbital abscess extending from right-sided rhinosinusitis, consistent with orbital cellulitis

shortlist.label: Cavernous sinus thrombosis
shortlist.why_kept: Severe headaches and signs of orbital and sinus involvement, with potential for cavernous sinus thrombosis

shortlist.label: Sphenoethmoidal sinusitis
shortlist.why_kept: CT scan showed orbital abscess extending from right-sided rhinosinusitis, and patient has purulent nasal secretions

shortlist.label: Pott's puffy tumor
shortlist.why_kept: Erosion into zygomatic bone and presence of orbital abscess, consistent with Pott's puffy tumor

shortlist.label: Invasive fungal sinusitis
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has poorly controlled diabetes mellitus, increasing risk for invasive fungal sinusitis, although cultures did not show fungus

raw.rationale: The patient's symptoms, including right-sided chemosis and exophthalmos, maxillary nerve hypoesthesia, and CT scan findings of an orbital abscess extending from right-sided rhinosinusitis, are consistent with orbital cellulitis. The presence of purulent nasal secretions and the growth of coagulase-negative Staphylococcus aureus and Enterococcus faecalis in cultures also support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Cavernous sinus thrombosis
rejected.why: There is no mention of symptoms or imaging findings suggestive of cavernous sinus thrombosis, such as bilateral eye findings or filling defects in the cavernous sinus on imaging.

rejected.label: Sphenoethmoidal sinusitis
rejected.why: While the patient has rhinosinusitis, the primary issue is the orbital abscess and cellulitis, which is not directly explained by sphenoethmoidal sinusitis alone.

rejected.label: Pott's puffy tumor
rejected.why: Pott's puffy tumor typically presents with a subperiosteal abscess and osteomyelitis of the frontal bone, which is not seen in this patient's imaging findings.

rejected.label: Invasive fungal sinusitis
rejected.why: The pathological tests showed no evidence of fungus, and the cultures grew bacterial pathogens, making invasive fungal sinusitis less likely.
